name: Lab 5.6 - Running-Light Tower
description: A maintained ENABLE selector and momentary STEP request drive a PLC-owned red -> amber -> green running-light sequence.

hints: PC supplies only raw tower_enable and momentary step_pulse; PLC owns sequence phase and all three color outputs.
Replace obsolete tower_step_active with tower_red, tower_amber and tower_green in older projects; one green output cannot walk three tiers.
The explicit original reference wraps green to red. Source specifies a pulse-driven sequence, without numeric timing or wrap detail. Separate Step presses need a released-input scan.

solution.summary: This is an original functional reference for the control concept, not a copy of the photographed solution.
steps: Default exercise editor is empty. Build PLC sequence logic or explicitly open .tools/plant-review-running-light-tower.rpproj.json after --audit-running-tower.
Run, then turn ENABLE to RUN. The first enabled accepted scan selects red; each fresh STEP edge advances amber, green, red.
Idle scans never advance. OFF clears lamps and phase on the next accepted scan; re-enable starts red. A simultaneous first-enable STEP is discarded.
solution.acceptance: Exactly one PLC color while enabled: red -> amber -> green -> red on separate Step edges. Disabled, held and unsampled repeated clicks cannot accumulate deferred advances.

machineGuide.purpose: A maintained ENABLE selector and momentary STEP request drive a PLC-owned red -> amber -> green running-light sequence.
startConditions: Built-in offline controller with user-authored or explicitly opened reference logic.
Initial ENABLE OFF, STEP released, phase zero and all lenses dark.
normalSequence: Default exercise editor is empty. Build PLC sequence logic or explicitly open .tools/plant-review-running-light-tower.rpproj.json after --audit-running-tower.
Run, then turn ENABLE to RUN. The first enabled accepted scan selects red; each fresh STEP edge advances amber, green, red.
Idle scans never advance. OFF clears lamps and phase on the next accepted scan; re-enable starts red. A simultaneous first-enable STEP is discarded.
stopBehavior: Stop clears PLC color commands and discards pending Step, retaining ENABLE and internal phase.
Run republishes the retained color; its first scan establishes a new Step edge baseline without advancing.
Application Reset clears requests and phase, returns ENABLE to OFF and leaves stopped scan zero; the next enable selects red.
faultBehavior: A missing or stale input must fail safe and remain diagnosable.
expectedObservations: Exactly one PLC color while enabled: red -> amber -> green -> red on separate Step edges. Disabled, held and unsampled repeated clicks cannot accumulate deferred advances.
